label: TMUA 2021 · Paper 1 · Question 19

hints.title: Bound the inner angle before solving
hints.body: The sine is applied to 4cosθ×60∘. First use the range of cosine and the fact that the exponential base is greater than one to bound this inner angle.
hints.recap: The range of an inner expression restricts which trigonometric branches can occur.
hints.pitfall: Read the expression as an exponential in the cosine, not as four times the cosine.
hints.pause: Find the smallest and largest possible inner angles.

recall.reminder: The range of an inner expression restricts which trigonometric branches can occur.

hints.title: Solve inside the permitted inner range
hints.body: Take both signs when passing from a squared sine to sine. List only the angle solutions that lie within the inner-angle bounds you found. Then undo the exponential to find the possible cosine values.
hints.recap: Solve a nested equation from the outside inward while carrying the allowed range.
hints.pitfall: Do not keep a sine-angle branch that the exponential expression cannot reach.
hints.pause: Recover all permitted values of the outer cosine.

recall.reminder: Solve a nested equation from the outside inward while carrying the allowed range.

hints.title: Order the outer angle solutions
hints.body: For each possible cosine value, find the nonnegative angle solutions and merge them into one increasing list. The interval endpoint must include the third distinct solution and exclude the fourth.
hints.recap: An inclusive upper endpoint changes the boundary cases in a root-count condition.
hints.pitfall: Count a repeated appearance of the same angle only once, and remember that zero is allowed.
hints.pause: Identify the third and fourth distinct angles and translate that into the required range for the endpoint.

recall.reminder: An inclusive upper endpoint changes the boundary cases in a root-count condition.

solution:
1. Bound the inner angle. Since −1≤cosθ≤1, we have 14≤4cosθ≤4, so 15∘≤4cosθ×60∘≤240∘.

2. Solve the inner sine equation. In this angle range, sin2u=34 has solutions u=60∘,120∘,240∘. Thus 4cosθ=1,2,4, giving cosθ=0,12,1.

3. Order the original angles. The nonnegative solutions begin θ=0∘,60∘,90∘,270∘,300∘,360∘,…. Exactly three lie in 0∘≤θ≤x∘ when the third is included and the fourth is excluded: 90≤x<270.

Answer B. At the lower boundary there are three solutions; at the excluded upper boundary there would be four.
knowledgePattern: Bound a nested trigonometric argument, solve its branches and locate the third and fourth angular solutions
